purpose: Resolve the late-morning/afternoon second US suppression cycle against the corrected 09:30 Marshall air/water-air state while submarine recontact forces limited TG58.2 schedule disruption.
historical_sanity: Historical FLINTLOCK used repeated carrier strikes through the day plus land-based support and later surface bombardment to keep Roi/Taroa/Wotje unusable. Branch defenders are warned, dispersed and more resilient, so the second cycle further degrades rather than instantly erases the network.

US_second_cycle.launch_and_attack_window: 10:45-14:40 local, staggered by recovery, refuel and submarine alarm rather than one simultaneous wave

target_split_center.mission: fighter sweep, radar/radio, runway repair parties, dispersed aircraft
fighter suppression, communications, runway, AA/aircraft dispersal
reduce the still-intact land-attack/night-strike reservoir before dusk

US_second_cycle.submarine_forcing: TG58.2 launch/recovery rhythm is delayed about 15-25 minutes and locally desynchronized by the recontact/ASW maneuver. This modestly reduces simultaneous fighter-sweep mass but does not cancel the strike.

Japanese_defense.Kyofu_low_medium_local_intercepts: 2-4 centered across southern/water nodes; subset of fighter total.
Japanese_defense.C2_state: Taroa/Roi begin the second cycle at degraded B/B+ and B states. Repeated radar/radio hits, fatigue and runway cratering reduce the Jan-28 exchange advantage; surviving plot/radio fragments still prevent total blindness at the start of the cycle.

cumulative_2Feb.guard: The 4 Japanese losses in the Jan31/Feb1 night attack are included only in the last figure.

base_effects.state_1630: Runway usable only in emergency windows; main radar/plot repeatedly interrupted; local visual/radio warning remains.
base_effects.repair: Night repair possible but daylight sustained sortie generation is badly reduced.

base_effects.state_1630: Primary fighter-direction and runway system heavily suppressed; small dispersed fighter remnant survives.
Ramps/fuel/maintenance points hit again; a small float-recon/Zuiun remnant remains usable from alternate lagoon points.
Runway and attack-aircraft support repeatedly hit; limited emergency/night use.
Gilbert land-air keeps pressure on runway and water support; local defense remains but high sortie rate is gone.
First serious same-day suppression reaches the land-attack reservoir. Runway cratered but patchable; dispersed bombers not annihilated.
base_effects.night_use: 4-6 aircraft could still be generated after repair if a fresh target track exists.

surface_followup: US cruisers/destroyers begin or prepare intermittent afternoon/evening bombardment of Taroa/Wotje runway and gun positions once air suppression allows, making runway repair a continuing contest rather than a one-time damage state.

operational_assessment.US: Second cycle succeeds in pushing Roi/Taroa below reliable fighter-direction quality and cuts the Eniwetok night-strike reservoir, at the cost of another roughly eleven irrecoverable aircraft centered. All three fast-carrier TGs remain combat operational.
operational_assessment.Japan: Marshall air system is no longer capable of meeting another full carrier cycle on equal warning terms, but it still retains scattered fighters, water reconnaissance and a small night-strike capability. Most importantly, the carrier-TG track remained fresh enough into early afternoon to preserve an operational decision rather than total blindness.

next_gate: Resolve late-afternoon/evening track freshness. If submarine/water-air contact can be refreshed again, decide a reduced land-based night strike and whether Shokaku/Zuikaku/Hiryu convert conditional closure into a 3-Feb dawn strike. If track ages, preserve the carrier force and prepare for amphibious approach.
